newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end listless trade mostly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: German shares end listless trade mostly unchanged.

text.p: German shares fell slightly in late IBIS trade on Thursday evening as the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street opened lower, but pared losses to end the day barely in positive territory.
The IBIS DAX index , which tracks electronic trade in 30 German blue-chips, ended virtually unchanged from its closing value on Tuesday, up only 1.88 points or 0.06 percent, at 3,212.82 points.
Earlier the DAX index of bourse trade ended the day down 2.62 percent at 3,215.24 points, after the index slid on the back of Wednesday's losses in electronic trade.

"There is very little cash business out there at the moment -- it's all futures driven. There are no real inflows and I don't imagine any real inflows until the important U.S. data comes out tomorrow," the broker said.
U.S. March payroll and unemployment figures are due on Friday at 1330 GMT.
A dealer in Frankfurt said many investors were taking advantage of lower share prices to hunt for bargains.
"There is bargain-hunting going on, with people using the lower levels to start buying. I think the index could keep going down and people will keep taking up bargains," he said.
One share which traded significantly higher than the overall market was the chemical giant BASF AG, which ended the day up 3.21 marks, 5.38 percent, at 62.90 marks.

Dealers said that positive sentiment towards the share was a delayed reaction to BASF's upbeat earnings outlook for 1997, reported on Wednesday, as well as initial positive feedback from the group's analysts' meeting.
